Criterion: acceptance test + 42 regression tests pass; delivery verified via audit log. All matrix arms: Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 5 (claude-sonnet-5). (1) Arm A, no memory (n=3): 3/3 pass; mean 137.3 tool calls, 48.3 grep/find, $7.20, 106.3 turns, 2123.6 s. Quality: works. Cost: works (about $7 and 35 min per feature run). (2) Arm B, cold store + tools + guidance, voluntary (n=2): pass; 0-1 voluntary writes across B and C (memory not used). Per-arm cost not reported (pooled below). Quality: works. Cost: works (pooled values). (3) Arm C, cold store + tools + proxy (n=3): pass. B+C+CS pooled (n=6, store cold in 5): 79.8 tool calls, 22.2 grep/find, $5.08, 77.0 turns, 1432.8 s (authors: prices the tool platform, not memory). Quality: works. Cost: works (pooled values). (4) Arm CS, seeded store + proxy (n=1): pass; 106 turns, $6.57, 1629 s; 5 injected / 236 correctly skipped of 241 decisions (262 requests). Quality: works. Cost: works. (5) Arm H, seeded store + native hooks (n=2): pass; H1 95 turns, $5.22, 1454 s; H2 102 turns, $6.09, 1187 s; gotcha fired on first touch, 0 false alarms in 40 and 35 evaluations. Quality: works. Cost: works. (6) Arm V, seeded store, hooks stripped, voluntary (n=1): pass; 114 turns, $6.23, 1297 s; 0 memory calls in 114 turns (seeded memory not used). Quality: works. Cost: works. Decay probe, Claude Code + Claude Haiku 4.5, 1 gated run each: (7) Arm N, no memory tier: k=108, 1,235 turns, $21.26; 106/108 summaries 0/10 facts; endpoint 10/10 but invalid (agent grepped harness session files against ban); audit completeness 0.93. Quality: does not work (facts unavailable at 106/108 boundaries; endpoint invalid). Cost: works ($21.26 for the whole probe). (8) Arm M, injected store via hooks: k=138, 1,489 turns, $28.94; 139 deliveries of all 10 facts (138/138 compact-resumes); endpoint 10/10 clean; audit completeness 0.70 (at 6k vs 8k read cap; task state still decayed into confabulated phases). Quality: works (all facts delivered at every boundary). Cost: partly ($28.94; delivery overhead ~240 tokens per injection, thrash guard forced a scrapped launch and a lower read cap)

fields.v: Matrix: one task on pinned Apache Camel checkout (SHA a543dc64); arms A, B, C, CS, H, V (12 graded runs: 9 pilot + 3 native-channel); baseline A (no memory) and V (seeded voluntary control for H). Held constant: agent product (Claude Code), model (Claude Sonnet 5), prompt, corpus SHA; launch posture asserted and archived. Acceptance: harness-provided acceptance test unmodified + 42 regression tests. Repetitions: 1-3 per arm; 6 further launches did not gate (aborts, operator pause, one invalidated). Decay probe: arms N vs M, one gated run each, Claude Haiku 4.5, compaction window pinned at 100k; read cap 8k (N) vs 6k (M), forced by thrash guard. Human intervention: none during runs stated except one operator pause and protocol repairs between launches

Correctness: all 12 pass, no difference. Seeded memory with knowledge held constant: H (95/102 turns, $5.22/$6.09) vs V (114 turns, $6.23) fewer turns and cheaper; wall time mixed (H1 1454 s, H2 1187 s vs V 1297 s); native hooks beat proxy CS (106 turns, $6.57, 1629 s) on every count; not significant ("none of this clears a significance bar"; ~15-20 runs per arm needed). Tool-equipped (pooled B+C+CS, n=6) vs vanilla A (n=3): -42% tool calls, -54% grep/find, -30% cost, -28% turns, -33% wall (platform effect, directional). Decay: M delivered all 10 facts at 138/138 boundaries vs N 0/10 at 106/108; M +21% turns and +36% cost; audit completeness 0.70 (M) vs 0.93 (N), confounded by read cap. No statistical tests

rev.why: Tool-equipped vs vanilla omitted two of the five reported deltas (total tool calls -42%, grep/find -54%); H vs V wall time is mixed (H1 1454 s > V 1297 s), which the draft's 'fewer turns and cheaper' did not show.

fields.v: Distinguished delivery mechanisms clearly (audit-logged fires, zero voluntary use); did not distinguish correctness (all pass); cost/turn differences directional only. Repeatability: small n (1-3 per arm, 1 per decay arm), within-arm wall spreads 2.4-4.4x. Limitations stated: token-match survival, synthetic facts, chars/4 token proxy, read-cap confound, unenforceable tool bans, one corpus/task/agent/model family, possible training-data contamination, author built both implementation and harness

Small samples; directional evidence only. Capture side unevaluated (notes seeded); symbol and temporal triggers never fired; audit completeness measure undercounts prose; read-cap confound; one corpus (Apache Camel), one task family, one agent product, one model family; decay probe uses small model (Haiku 4.5), larger summarizers may differ; Camel in training data. Future: capture-side automation; index budget ranking limitation logged as product work
